question.text: Suresh has the following investments and expenses in FY 2024-25 under the old tax regime: PPF contribution Rs.1,00,000; ELSS investment Rs.80,000; life insurance premium Rs.30,000; NPS contribution under Section 80CCD(1B) Rs.50,000; tuition fees for two children Rs.60,000. What is his total deduction under Sections 80C, 80CCE, and 80CCD(1B) combined?

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 80CCE caps the aggregate deduction under Sections 80C + 80CCC + 80CCD(1) at Rs.1,50,000. Suresh's 80C-eligible items already exceed this cap on the strength of PPF (Rs.1,00,000) + ELSS (Rs.80,000) + life insurance premium (Rs.30,000) = Rs.2,10,000, which is reduced to the Rs.1,50,000 ceiling. Section 80CCD(1B) provides a separate Rs.50,000 deduction for NPS contribution, over and above the 80CCE cap. Total = Rs.1,50,000 + Rs.50,000 = Rs.2,00,000. The Trap: Rs.3,20,000 adds every item without applying any cap. Rs.1,50,000 forgets the additional 80CCD(1B) benefit. Rs.2,70,000 sums all 80C-eligible items without applying the 80CCE ceiling, then adds 80CCD(1B). Note: The answer is unchanged whether or not tuition fees are counted, because the other listed 80C items already exceed Rs.1,50,000. The key takeaway is the 80CCE cap and the separate 80CCD(1B) deduction.
